text:
maria: Hey folks — noticed a perf regression on the INT8 AWQ path after the packing change. p95 for chat flows jumped ~20% when group_size=32. Sharing quick traces and numbers, wondering if this is a kernel-routing or unpack stall.

maria: Perf summary: model=redwood-7b-awq, cfg: group=32, pack=true, prefetch=on, batch=1
- baseline (group=16): p50=18ms, p95=46ms
- regression (group=32): p50=22ms, p95=56ms

maria: Flamegraph from perf-bot: https://perf.example/redwood/2124689012/flame.html
perf-bot: attached flamegraph and CPU sample rates for the run, sampled at 99hz. Hot functions: awq_unpack(), kv_cache_lookup(), kernel_dispatch_int8_group32().

aj: saw that earlier. Two quick hypotheses: 1) group32 forces kernel with serial unpack path that is not vectorized; 2) increasing cache misses due to larger prefetch window. Could also be increased memcpy churn from packing buffer growth.

kevin: +1 on memcpy. I instrumented allocator yesterday; observed higher malloc churn when group > 24 for some models (temp buffers). Likely packing creates temporary slab objects that miss L1.

olivia: Repro steps? Is this only with batch=1 latency flows or also throughput tests? If it's batch=1 latency critical path, the kernel chooser might prefer a higher throughput kernel with worse single-thread latency.

maria: Good point. This was single-convo latency (batch=1). Throughput runs (batch=8) actually saw small win for group32. So it's a latency single-request regression.

dmitri: Can you paste the kernel selection lines from telemetry? That tells which kernel variants we fell into.

maria: telemetry lines:
```
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] kernel_select: model=redwood-7b, seq=128, group=32 => kernel=int8_group32_serial_unroll
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] kernel_select: fallback_kernels=[int8_group16_simd, fp16_group32]
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] batch_heuristic: choose_unroll_for_batch1=true
```

aj: There it is — serial_unroll path. That kernel prioritizes packing density over per-token latency. For chat we should choose the SIMD-friendly group16 kernel.

kevin: Also check kv cache hotpath. Pack/unpack increased time spent in kv_cache_lookup by ~30% according to the flamegraph. Maybe packing alignment causes extra pointer chasing.

olivia: Quick experiment: try running with pack_align=64 and group=32; that may reduce misalignment. Or run with pack=false to confirm pure unpack cost.

maria: Ran pack=false locally: p95 dropped back to 47ms (close to baseline). So packing is the main contributor.

dmitri: Two action items: a) short-term: change batch_heuristic so batch=1 forces kernel=int8_group16_simd even when group=32 config; b) long-term: optimize int8_group32_serial_unroll to reduce memcpy/unpack. Who can own (b)?

aj: I can take (a) — quick config tweak in runtime chooser and a canary test.

kevin: I'll profile the serial_unroll kernel and add microbench for unpack memcpy sizes. I suspect we can memcpy into 64-byte aligned slab to drop L1 misses.

olivia: For the canary, also validate quality/regressions — we need to ensure changing chooser doesn't affect model quality (it shouldn't). Add perf bot monitor and rollout windows.

maria: Thanks. I'll open a short issue with traces and attach reproducer: https://tickets.redwood/INT8-REGRESS-234

perf-bot: canary created: runtime-chooser/awq-group16-latency-fix; monitor p50/p95 across canary endpoints for 2 hours.

aj: patch ready locally, will push to canary in ~30m. Command I used to test locally:
```
./run_infer.sh --model redwood-7b-awq --group-size 32 --pack true --batch 1 --chooser-override group16-for-latency
```

maria: after aj's patch on canary: p95 is back to 45ms, p50=19ms. No quality diffs in automated evals.

kevin: Great. For long-term kernel work, I'll add a perf PR with lower-level changes: reduce unpack buffer copies, use prefetch for kv cache lines, and try a small SIMD fallback in serial_unroll. Will bench across group sizes 8/16/32.

dmitri: Please include microbench harness output in PR with raw cycles and memcpy bytes. Ideally show perf counters: L1d_miss, LLC_miss, cycles.

maria: assigning owners in the ticket: aj->chooser tweak, kevin->kernel optim, olivia->canary validation, dmitri->bench harness. Will follow up in the ticket thread.

aj: quick note — adding a chooser override is safe as a stopgap. We should also add telemetry flag that surfaces when batch=1 but chooser selects a serial kernel so we can alert proactively.

maria: agreed. Thanks everyone :thumbsup!
